title: kbmon --events: ops rows, coord events and delivery outcomes as event and span records with id-only attributes
goal: python3 _tools/kbmon.py --events [--since CURSOR] prints one JSON object with a cursor, the events (coord events, done.refused rows and query-log delivery outcomes) and the spans (each landing with a child span per land.step, each agent.run, each test.run and each delivery whose time the log gives) newer than the cursor, each with times in Unix nanoseconds and attributes that are numbers, flags or ids that passed redact.redact; a second call with the returned cursor repeats none of them

clauses.clause: python3 _tools/kbmon.py --events [--since CURSOR] prints one JSON object with a cursor, the events (coord events, done.refused rows and query-log delivery outcomes) and the spans (each landing with a child span per land.step, each agent.run, each test.run and each delivery whose time the log gives) newer than the cursor, each with times in Unix nanoseconds and attributes that are numbers, flags or ids that passed redact.redact
a second call with the returned cursor repeats none of them

gates.question: What does the --events cursor hold?
options: the newest spool row time and coord sequence, as one opaque text
gates.recommendation: the newest spool row time and coord sequence, as one opaque text
gates.answer: the newest spool row time and coord sequence, as one opaque text

notes: Plan 2026-10-18: kbmon stays read-only, so the cursor is the caller's to keep. coord event fields are ids by coord.py's own rule, and id-shaped fake secrets (IDS in the check) pass it, so the redaction is proved on them. Plan 2026-10-18: reuses mon_log.py's reader of coord events and ops rows; the cursor and the span records are this item's.
